import Diagram from '../../../components/Diagram.astro';

<span class="status status--decided">decided</span>

No implementation code gets written until its behaviour is defined. The source of truth is:

- **Gherkin `.feature` files** describing behaviour in plain language
- **JSON test vectors** generated from them: an initial state, plus per-client operation streams delivered late and out of order

## One suite, every implementation

<Diagram name="13-verification" alt="Verification: feature files feed a fuzzer that emits JSON vectors; vectors run through the Xmesh harness and its invariant checks, and SHA-256 hashes of canonical XML are compared across delivery orders; a later native C++ rewrite is held to the same vectors; for M1 the same vectors are replayed by CLI peers through a Rust tracker over WebSocket, with forced disconnects." />

| Harness | Why it exists |
| --- | --- |
| **Xmesh on Yrs** (`cargo test`) | The implementation. Every vector is replayed in many delivery orders. |
| **Native C++ Xmesh** | *Later spike.* Held to the same vectors and cross-checked against Xmesh on Yrs. |

The pass conditions are **invariants**, checked on every run:

- **Convergence:** every delivery order ends with the same **SHA-256 of the canonical XML**.
- **No cycles:** the materialised tree is always a tree.
- **Idempotence:** delivering an operation twice changes nothing.


## The fuzzer

The first task from the original handover, re-scoped to feed every harness. It generates:

- an initial SVG (a root `<svg>` with one `<g>` layer)
- randomised operations from several clients: inserting paths, updating attributes, moving nodes, adding comments
- one chronological stream per client, plus heavily delayed and shuffled delivery orders

## Over a real network

[Milestone M1](/build/milestones/) runs the same vectors through two CLI peers and a Rust tracker, all embedding Xmesh, over WebSocket, including dropped connections and reconnect sync. Convergence then holds over a real, unreliable network, not just in a test process.
